method: Warm-land colour threshold locates the skyline and last land row; median across seven columns at each stored profile sample. Colours are local patch medians and the linear-RGB mean of a centre-third strip. These approximate display-space measurements do not test radiometric accuracy; a single wave realization need not equal the statistical sea average. The waterline is compared with the nominal horizon, not a full terrain-and-wave intersection solution.
evidence: Computational display-space comparison plus visual inspection, not physical validation of the generated image.
selection: First IC-1 illustration, with outstanding colour and physical-rendering limits recorded in ic-1-final-review.json.

visual_review.framing: Low viewing position and broad coast profile retained. Measured maximum skyline discrepancy is 5.93 pixels at 1080px image height. Waterline is 44.95% down versus the nominal 45.34% horizon; the comparison does not solve wave/shore intersection.
visual_review.lighting: Visible slopes are broadly front-lit, consistent with the 54.2-degree-high Sun behind the viewer. No visible Sun, Earth, stars or false direct-sun glitter path. Absolute illuminance cannot be inferred from a generated display image.
visual_review.shadows: Shallow relief shadows have diffuse fill rather than black interiors or long low-Sun shadows. Their precise geometry and direction are not validated: local relief is generated and the guide has no cast-shadow solution.
visual_review.atmosphere: Pale cyan upper sky and paler cream-green near-horizon gradient retained, with gently reduced distant-land contrast. The selected sky remains slightly darker than the reference. Haze is an illustrative rendering of the supplied transmittance, not a solved scattering image.
visual_review.wave_structure: The broad undulations and finer ripples are inherited from the projected domain-wave guide and water component. Broad wave scale decreases with distance; no breaking surf or foam was introduced. The guide, not the generated image, has a measured Hs of 1.223 m and peak wavelength of 33.111 m. A single picture does not validate Hs, period, mean-square slope or propagation direction.
visual_review.colour: Foreground centre-third strip encodes to #525e5c, close to the #505e5b target. Middle water at 8 degrees down remains #626f6e versus #788883, and the near-horizon water has a slight blue bias. Wave-facet variation and the statistical source mean differ, but this residual mismatch is not dismissed as proof of agreement.
visual_review.materials_and_detail: Terrain rebuilt after earlier waxy-looking generations. The selected version has more irregular matte rock/regolith detail. Only the broad silhouette is constrained; internal rock forms and slope details are illustrative and can depart from the source DEM.
visual_review.composition: No obvious mask seams, inserted panels or disconnected coast/water geometry at the full frame view. Water texture remains generated rather than a pixel-exact domain render. Shore reflections and wave/terrain occlusion are not solved by these guides.
visual_review.ecology: The omission of visible plants is the optical-study placeholder stated in the revised scene text. Productive water composition is a biosphere design guess. This image is not a depiction of an established mature barren world.
visual_review.image_content: No visible text, numbers, scene labels, watermarks, borders, UI, clouds, celestial disks, people, craft or buildings.

remaining_limits: Middle-water average remains darker than the scene swatch; sky and near-horizon water also differ modestly.
Generated terrain microgeometry and wave phases are illustrative, not measured geography or solved water geometry.
Cast shadows, full spectral transport, terrain reflections, and wave visibility above the flat-horizon guide were not computed.
The wave spectrum is the study's borrowed Nectaris case, not a validated local Ingenii sea state.
Native output is 1672 by 941; no artificial upscaling or claim of native 4K.
